educators.title: For educators
educators.heroTitle: Run a Thinkerwell lesson with your group
educators.heroBody: Use Thinkerwell's free lessons with your group. Choose one course, several courses, or lessons from different courses. Teach on one shared screen, in pairs or on separate devices, or print the lessons. No learner accounts are needed.
educators.pilotAboutBody: What Thinkerwell offers, what you need to run a group, and how learners' privacy is kept.
educators.pilotCodesBody: A card with a code for each learner to use instead of their name, and a list for you to keep.
educators.pilotDayBody: One page for the adults running a session: before, during and after, and what to do if something goes wrong.
educators.need1: One device for every 1 to 3 learners, or one big screen
educators.need4: Internet for the first visit, and for videos
educators.step1Body: Choose one course, several, or lessons from different courses. Lessons can go in any order. Choose ones that fit your group, or follow the numbers.
educators.step2Body: Learners read, write about what they read and talk it through in pairs. Watch is optional.
educators.step3Body: Ask two or three learners to share their answer. Everyone writes one reflection.
educators.answerKeyLabel: Answer key for the {section} section check
educators.feedbackBody: Something confusing, too difficult or broken? Tell us at {email}. Don't send learners' names or written answers.
educators.toolsIntro: Progress stays on the device it was made on.
educators.classBody: Lessons finished and where each learner is now. No scores.
educators.certificatesBody: Every certificate earned on this device, one to a page.
educators.guidesBody: A teacher guide for every lesson in every course, with a session plan and the answers; every lesson ready to print; and an answer key for each section check.
educators.groupIntro: Everything here prints on A4, in black and white.
educators.feedbackSheetBody: One sheet for each group: which courses and lessons you used, how it went, and what to fix. You fill it in by hand.

organisations.title: Use Thinkerwell with your learners
organisations.intro: Thinkerwell offers free social studies courses and educator resources for youth across Southeast Asia. Use them with a group on shared devices or in print. Explore the courses and teaching materials, or get in touch about using Thinkerwell in your learning space.
organisations.honesty: Thinkerwell is a student-led platform. It is not a registered charity or nonprofit.
organisations.whatBody: Four courses for learners aged about 10 to 17. Exploring Our World: {ourWorld} lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life. Digital World: {digitalWorld} lessons about AI and the digital world. Southeast Asia Through Time: {southeastAsia} lessons about the region's past, from real objects, maps and letters. Art, Architecture and Society: {art} lessons about works and buildings from around the world. Most lessons have five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect (four where a lesson has no video, as every lesson does in Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu and Tiếng Việt). It runs in a web browser on shared laptops and tablets, in English, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu or Tiếng Việt. Lessons work offline once a course is saved on the device; the optional videos need the internet.
organisations.get1: All four courses, free. No accounts, no ads, and nothing locked.
organisations.get2: A teacher guide for every lesson, answer keys for the section checks, and every lesson ready to print.
organisations.get3: A checklist for setting up each device, learner code cards and a one-page session guide for staff.
organisations.get4: Answers to your questions, and changes to the course based on what you tell us.
organisations.askTitle: What you need to run a group
organisations.ask1: An educator or volunteer to lead each session.
organisations.ask2: Some laptops or tablets with a web browser. Learners can share them.
organisations.ask4: The internet for the first visit on each device, and for the optional videos.
organisations.privacy1: Learners can use codes instead of names. Each learner gets a code card, like ABC-01, and types the code as their name. Only you keep the list that matches codes to names.
organisations.privacy2: No accounts, no email addresses and no ads. Learners' writing stays on the device they use, and voice recordings never leave it.
organisations.privacyNow: Learners' work and progress stay on the device they use, and are not sent to Thinkerwell. Online speech-to-text is off unless your staff turn it on; when it is on, what learners say goes to the browser maker's service. We will tell you before anything else changes.
organisations.privacy4: Videos are optional. They play from YouTube, only when a learner taps play, and every video has a written version.
organisations.startBody: Set up each device before the first session, and print what you need.
organisations.contactBody: Ask a question, or tell us about your organisation: where you are, and about how many learners would use Thinkerwell.
organisations.pilotNote: Thinkerwell’s initial pilot is for selected partner organisations. Lessons, timing, feedback, any data collection and required permissions are agreed directly with each organisation before its pilot begins.

codeCards.title: Code cards
codeCards.intro: Each learner gets a code to type as their name, so their real name is never on the device. Choose a short prefix for your group and the number of learners. You get cards to cut out, and a list to write names on.
codeCards.prefixHelper: 2 to 5 letters or numbers, for example ABC.
codeCards.summary: {count} cards, from {first} to {last}. Print on A4 and cut along the dashed lines.
codeCards.cardHow: Tap “{tile}” and type this code as your name.
codeCards.listIntro: Write each learner's name next to their code. Keep this list safe with your staff. Don't type names into Thinkerwell, and don't send this list to anyone.

teacherGuide.intro: Everything you need to teach this lesson, with the answers. It prints on A4, black on white, without the menus.
teacherGuide.contentNotePointer: The video has a content note. Read it before class: it is with the video, below.
teacherGuide.planIntro: A suggested plan for a session of about 45 minutes. Change it to suit your group.
teacherGuide.planShorter: Only 30 minutes? Use the 30 min column: skip Watch or read instead, and take a little time off the other steps. Learners can open Watch later, because nothing is locked.
teacherGuide.planShorterNoWatch: Only 30 minutes? Use the 30 min column: take a little time off each step.
teacherGuide.planOtherLanguages: In Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu and Tiếng Việt, a lesson has no Watch step unless it has a video in that language. Open this guide in that language to see its plan.

planDo.warmUp: Ask the warm-up question. Every answer is fine: it gets everyone thinking.

read.one: Read the text in Standard or Simpler English. Look at the evidence and the picture together.
read.other: Read the {count} parts one at a time, in Standard or Simpler English. Look at the evidence and the picture together.

check.one: Learners answer the quick-check question, then talk about the answer.
check.other: Learners answer the {count} quick-check questions, then talk about the answers.

planDo.write: Learners plan and write their answer, then tick the self-check. Sentence starters help.
planDo.speak: Learners tell a partner their answer, or practise on their own.
planDo.watch: Watch the video together, or read the written version instead.
planDo.reflect: Everyone answers the first reflect question. It finishes the lesson.

teacherGuide.checkIntro: Learners see the options in a different order, and can try again as often as they like.
teacherGuide.think: Think question: there is no single right answer.
teacherGuide.thinkOptional: Think question, optional: there is no single right answer.
teacherGuide.exampleNote: One way to answer. Learners' answers can be different.
teacherGuide.discussIntro: Questions from the lesson to talk about together. Let anyone pass.
teacherGuide.reflectRequired: Learners answer this one to finish the lesson.
teacherGuide.videoOffline: The video needs the internet. The written version (Read instead) works offline and has the same ideas.
teacherGuide.afterVideo: After the video or the reading
teacherGuide.sourcesIntro: The lesson is written in Thinkerwell's own words, drawing on these sources. Use them to check a fact or to find out more (they are in English).

answerKey.title: Answer key: {section}
answerKey.intro: Every question in this section check, with the answers. It prints on A4, black on white, without the menus.
answerKey.practice: The section check is for practice. It never blocks learners: there is no time limit, they can try again as often as they like, and every lesson stays open whatever their score.
answerKey.order: Learners see the options in a different order, so talk about the answer itself, not where it sits.
answerKey.question: Question {n} · {skill}

setup.title: Set up this device
setup.intro: Do these steps once on each laptop or tablet. Each step says whether it's done on this device.
setup.paperIntro: On each device, open Thinkerwell, then For educators, then Set up this device. Tick each step when it's done.

homeScreen.title: Add Thinkerwell to the home screen

why.one: Then it opens like an app. On iPad and iPhone, this also stops Safari deleting saved work after {count} day without a visit.
why.other: Then it opens like an app. On iPad and iPhone, this also stops Safari deleting saved work after {count} days without a visit.

homeScreen.first: Do this first. Then open Thinkerwell from the home screen, and do the other steps there.
homeScreen.installed: Thinkerwell is open from the home screen.
homeScreen.inBrowser: Thinkerwell is open in the browser. If you've added it already, open it from the home screen instead.

apple.name: iPad or iPhone (Safari)
apple.step2: Tap Share: the square with an arrow pointing up.
apple.step3: Tap Add to Home Screen. You may need to scroll down to find it.
apple.step5: Open Thinkerwell from its icon. It keeps its own saved work, apart from Safari, so add learners there.

android.name: Android tablet or phone (Chrome)
android.step2: Tap the menu: the three dots at the top.
android.step3: Tap Add to home screen, or Install app.

desktop.name: Windows laptop or Chromebook (Chrome or Edge)
desktop.step1: Open Thinkerwell in Chrome or Edge.
desktop.step2: Click the install button at the end of the address bar. If there isn't one, open the menu: the three dots.
desktop.step3: Choose Install Thinkerwell. In the menu it may be under Cast, save and share, or under Apps.

offline.title: Download the course for offline use
offline.why: Then every lesson works without the internet. Only the videos need it.
offline.how: Open Thinkerwell with the internet on, and keep it open until the lessons are saved. It does this by itself.
offline.audio: For Listen without the internet, also download the lesson audio: in Settings, under Lesson audio.
offline.courses: If your group will use the other courses, also save them: in Settings, under Courses for offline use. A course you only open is saved as far as you went.
offline.coursesOpen: Courses for offline use in Settings

storage.title: Keep saved work safe
storage.why: Otherwise the browser may delete learners' work when the device is low on space.
storage.how: Tap Keep work safe. If the browser asks, choose Allow.
storage.checking: Checking what the browser does with saved work…
storage.done: The browser keeps saved work on this device, even when space runs low.
storage.todo: The browser may delete saved work when space runs low.
storage.refused: The browser said no for now. Browsers often agree once Thinkerwell is on the home screen and used for a few days. Try again then.
storage.unsupported: This browser can't be asked. Adding Thinkerwell to the home screen helps keep work safe.
storage.noStorage: This browser window can't save learners' work at all. A private window can cause this. Open Thinkerwell in a normal window.

learners.title: Add the learners who use this device
learners.why: Each learner gets a tile on the home page, and their work is kept apart.
learners.how: Tap Add a learner, or let each learner tap I'm new here on the home page.
learners.codes: Using code cards? Each learner types their code as their name.
learners.none: No learners on this device yet.

voice.title: Choose the Listen voice (optional)
voice.why: Listen reads lessons aloud with the best voice it finds on the device. You can hear each voice and choose another, or download a clearer one.
voice.whyRecorded: Listen plays recordings of a natural voice. Where a recording isn't on the device and there's no internet, it reads with the best voice it finds on the device. You can hear each voice and choose another, or download a clearer one.
voice.how: In Settings, under Listen voice, play a sample and choose the clearest voice.
voice.automatic: Listen reads with {voice}, the best voice on this device.
voice.chosen: Listen reads with {voice}, chosen in Settings.
voice.none: This device has no voice that Listen can use, so Listen doesn't show. Settings says how to add one.
voice.noneRecorded: This device has no voice of its own that Listen can use, so Listen plays only the recordings. Settings says how to add a voice.

speech.title: Check speech to text
speech.why: Say it lets learners talk instead of typing. The check tells lessons whether it can work here.
speech.last: Do this step last. On some tablets the check has closed the browser tab. If that happens, open Thinkerwell again.
speech.how: In Settings, under Say it, tap Check this device.
speech.notChecked: Not checked on this device yet.
speech.onDevice: Speech to text works on this device, and what learners say is not sent anywhere.
speech.download: It needs a one-time download first. In Settings, tap Download speech to text on good Wi-Fi, then check again.
speech.notOnDevice: This browser can't do it on the device, so Say it stays hidden. Learners type instead.
speech.none: This browser can't turn speech into text, so there's nothing to check. Say it stays hidden, and learners type instead.

later.title: Before you reset this device or give it back
later.body: In Settings, choose All learners on this device, save the work to a file, then load the file on the next device. Recordings aren't in the file. Keep the file safe: anyone with it can read the work.
later.open: Save work to a file in Settings

classView.title: The class on this device
classView.intro: Every learner on this device, by name, and what each one has done.
classView.noScores: There are no scores here, because anyone using this device can open this page.
classView.empty: No learners on this device yet.
classView.emptyBody: Learners show up here once they're added. Each learner can add themselves with I'm new here on the home page.
classView.noStorage: This browser window can't keep learners' work, so there's nothing to show here. A private window can cause this.

allCertificates.title: All certificates

count.one: {count} certificate earned on this device. It prints on a landscape page of its own.
count.other: {count} certificates earned on this device. Each prints on a landscape page of its own.

allCertificates.names: Names come from this device and can't be changed here. To print a different name, choose that learner, then open their certificate from the course page.
allCertificates.empty: Nobody on this device has a certificate yet.
allCertificates.emptyBody: A learner gets one by finishing every lesson in a section. The section check isn't needed.

settings.title: Settings for this device
settings.intro: These settings are for teachers and volunteers. They apply to everyone who uses this device, and they stay on it.
settings.moreTitle: For educators setting up this device
settings.moreIntro: Moving work to another device, the Listen voice, lesson audio for offline use and speech-to-text.
settings.noStorage: This browser window can't save settings.
settings.saveFailed: That change couldn't be saved. Try again.

language.title: Language
language.label: Language on this device
language.help: Everything shows in this language at once: buttons, instructions and, in Indonesian, Malay and Vietnamese, the lessons too. It is kept for this device, for the first page and anyone who hasn't chosen who's learning.
language.helpLearner: Everything shows in this language at once: buttons, instructions and, in Indonesian, Malay and Vietnamese, the lessons too. It is kept for {name}, and changes back when someone else is chosen.

offline.title: Offline and data
offline.checking: Checking whether the lessons are saved on this device…
offline.preparing: Saving the lessons on this device for offline use. Keep Thinkerwell open, with the internet on, until this says they're saved.
offline.ready: All {count} lessons are saved on this device, with their pictures. Thinkerwell works here without the internet, except the videos.
offline.failed: The lessons didn't finish saving for offline use. Open Thinkerwell again with the internet on, and it tries again.
offline.unsupported: This browser can't keep the lessons for offline use, so Thinkerwell needs the internet here. A private window can cause this.
offline.saveDataHelp: Turns the videos off, so Watch opens on the written version, which has the same ideas. Everything else already works without the internet.
offline.saveDataFromBrowser: It's on because this device is set to save data.

reading.title: Reading and listening
reading.levelHelp: Lessons open in this level for anyone who hasn't chosen one yet. Learners can switch in any lesson, and their choice is kept.
reading.speedHelp: How fast Listen reads aloud. Learners can change it while listening.
reading.noVoice: This browser has no voice on this device, so Listen doesn't show here.

listenVoice.title: Listen voice
listenVoice.intro: Listen reads lessons aloud with a voice that works on this device, so nothing is sent online. Some voices sound clearer than others: play a sample, then choose.
listenVoice.introRecorded: Listen plays recordings of a natural voice, made for every lesson. Where a part's recording isn't on this device and there's no internet, it reads with a voice of this device instead, so nothing is sent online. Choose that voice here.
listenVoice.deviceVoice: Device voice, when there's no recording
listenVoice.sampleUnavailable: The sample isn't on this device yet, and the device has no voice to read it with. Connect to the internet and try again.
listenVoice.noVoice: This device has no English voice that Listen can use, so Listen doesn't show. The steps below add one.
listenVoice.noVoiceRecorded: This device has no English voice. Listen still plays the recordings, but can't read a part whose recording isn't on this device while there's no internet. The steps below add a voice.
listenVoice.noVoiceIndonesian: This device has no Indonesian voice yet, so Listen can't read Indonesian lessons. The steps below add one.
listenVoice.noVoiceIndonesianRecorded: This device has no Indonesian voice. Listen still plays the recordings, but can't read a part whose recording isn't on this device while there's no internet. The steps below add a voice.
listenVoice.noVoiceMalay: This device has no Malay voice yet, so Listen can't read Malay lessons. The steps below add one.
listenVoice.noVoiceVietnamese: This device has no Vietnamese voice yet, so Listen can't read Vietnamese lessons. The steps below add one.
listenVoice.noVoiceMalayRecorded: This device has no Malay voice. Listen still plays the recordings, but can't read a part whose recording isn't on this device while there's no internet. The steps below add a voice.

better.title: Get a clearer voice
better.intro: Most devices can download better voices for free. Voices can be large, so use good Wi-Fi. Then open this page again and choose the new voice.

apple.name: iPad or iPhone
apple.steps: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Spoken Content (called Read & Speak on newer versions), then Voices. Choose English, Indonesian, Malay or Vietnamese, then a voice marked Enhanced or Premium, and download it.
apple.note: Safari doesn't let websites use every voice you download. If the new voice isn't in the list above, keep the one you have.

android.name: Android tablet or phone
android.steps: Open Settings and search for text-to-speech. Next to Preferred engine, tap the settings button, then Install voice data. Choose English, Indonesian, Malay or Vietnamese, then download a voice.

windows.name: Windows laptop
windows.steps: Open Settings, then Time & language, then Speech. Next to Manage voices, choose Add voices, then English (United Kingdom), Indonesian, Malay or Vietnamese. You may need an administrator account. Then close the browser and open it again.

chromebook.name: Chromebook
chromebook.steps: Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Text-to-Speech, then Text-to-Speech voice settings. Install the voices for English, Indonesian, Malay or Vietnamese.

courseFiles.title: Courses for offline use
courseFiles.intro: Our World is saved on this device after the first visit. The other courses are saved as they are opened. To use all of them without the internet, save them here, on good Wi-Fi. This saves the pages, lessons and pictures. Videos always need the internet, and the lesson audio is saved separately, below.
courseFiles.statePart: {course}: partly saved. Save the rest to open every lesson offline ({size} MB in all).
courseFiles.savedAll: All the courses are on this device. They open without the internet.
courseFiles.stopped: Stopped. What was saved stays on this device.
courseFiles.failed: Some files didn't save. Check the connection and try again. What was saved stays.
courseFiles.saveData: Save data is on, so nothing downloads from here. Turn Save data off above to save the courses.
courseFiles.notReady: This can start once the site is saved on this device for offline use, above.
courseFiles.unsupported: This browser can't keep the courses, so they need the internet here.

about.title: About Thinkerwell
about.tagline: Free social studies learning for youth across Southeast Asia, especially those facing barriers to education.
about.missionBody: Thinkerwell began with a love of social studies and a question: how can more youth have the chance to explore the world they live in? We built a free digital platform to make digital learning tools and social studies education accessible to youth facing barriers to education. Our goal is to help learners ask questions, grow their critical thinking skills, explore diverse perspectives, and share their own ideas.

explore.title: Explore your world
explore.blurb: Two minutes on why we built Thinkerwell and what's in it.
explore.p1: Every learner deserves the chance to explore the world they live in. But across Southeast Asia, many youth face barriers to education. In Myanmar, about 3.8 million people are displaced inside their own country. In Malaysia, refugee children can't attend government schools. And in East Asia and the Pacific, one in three school-age children had no internet at home.
explore.p2: Where schools are stretched, lessons often stick to the basics: reading, maths, and skills for a job. Those matter. But there's little room left for the skills that open up the world: thinking critically, communicating with evidence, and taking other perspectives.
explore.p3: Research backs this up. In a Stanford study, students who learned history by questioning real sources grew more in historical thinking, reading, and knowledge than students in regular classes.
explore.p4: That's why we built Thinkerwell: free lessons in social studies and beyond, for youth facing barriers to education. Our first course, Exploring Our World, has 24 lessons in history, geography, culture, and civic life, and every lesson has five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect. Every reading has a simpler version and can be read aloud, and lessons work offline, in several languages.
explore.p5: Thinkerwell doesn't replace teachers. It lightens their load, with a ready-made guide for every lesson, plus answer keys and printables.
explore.p6: Our goal is to help learners ask questions, grow their critical thinking skills, explore diverse perspectives, and share their own ideas. Thinkerwell. Social studies and beyond. Explore your world.
explore.sources: Sources: UNHCR (2026); UNICEF and ITU (2020); Reisman, Stanford (2012).

session.title: Run a session
session.blurb: A Thinkerwell lesson with a group, from start to finish, in about a minute.
session.p1: You don't need accounts, passwords or a big budget to run a Thinkerwell lesson. Here's a session, from start to finish.
session.p2: Before the first session, set up each tablet or laptop once, with the checklist under For educators. Thinkerwell saves the lessons on the device, so they work without the internet.
session.p3: Learners can share a device. Each one taps their name, and their work stays on that device.
session.p4: Pick any lesson. Its teacher guide has a plan for 30 or 45 minutes, with the answers. Then learners work through five steps. They read, in standard or simpler English. They write. They talk it through with a partner. They watch a short video, or read it instead. And they reflect.
session.p5: Afterwards, see where every learner is up to. There are no scores, just lessons finished. No devices that day? Every lesson and teacher guide prints in black and white.
session.p6: Thinkerwell is free, with no ads. Social studies and beyond. Everything for teachers is at thinkerwell.app, under For educators.

setup.title: Set up a device
setup.blurb: The checklist, step by step, in about a minute.
setup.p1: Before the first session, set up each laptop or tablet once. Here's how. Open thinkerwell.app, tap For educators, then Set up this device. The checklist says which steps are already done on this device.
setup.p2: First, add Thinkerwell to the home screen, so it opens like an app. The checklist shows the steps for your kind of device. On an iPad, this also stops Safari deleting saved work.
setup.p3: Then open Thinkerwell from its icon, with the internet on, and keep it open while the lessons are saved. After that, every lesson works offline. Next, tap Keep work safe, so the browser keeps learners' work, even when space runs low.
setup.p4: Add the learners who use the device. Each one gets a tile on the home page. Using code cards? Learners type their code as their name.
setup.p5: In Settings, you can choose the voice that reads lessons aloud. Do the speech check last: under Say it, tap Check this device.
setup.p6: Before you reset a device or give it back, save everyone's work to a file, and load it on the next one. The checklist prints on one page, so you can tick it off on paper. Thinkerwell. Social studies and beyond.

aboutPage.researchNote: Research on content-rich literacy, writing from memory, self-explanation, purposeful video, and guided reflection informs this design.
aboutPage.researchIntro: These studies examine related learning activities in different settings. They inform individual design choices; they have not evaluated Thinkerwell or established that our exact five-step sequence improves outcomes.

studies.read: A randomized trial with children from kindergarten to grade 4 found that a program teaching reading through science and social studies helped them learn more of both. It tested a whole program, not reading alone, with younger learners in a different setting.
studies.write: Students who wrote what they remembered, as an essay or by free recall, did better on a later test than students who took notes or highlighted. What helped was recalling the ideas: writing an essay did no better than free recall.
studies.speak: In a small science study, grade 8 students who were asked to explain a text to themselves understood it better than students who read it twice. It supports explaining your thinking, not any kind of talking.
studies.watch: Short tests between the parts of an online lecture helped students keep their attention and learn more. It tested questions during lectures, not every kind of video.
studies.reflect: During a middle-school science unit, the kind of reflection prompt students were given was linked to how well they understood the topic. It compared kinds of prompts; it did not test Thinkerwell's reflection questions.

privacy.title: Privacy & Child Safeguarding
privacy.intro: Thinkerwell provides free social studies learning for youth across Southeast Asia. We are committed to respecting learners’ privacy, dignity and safety. This policy covers our website, communications and learning activities. Its safeguarding commitments apply to everyone under 18 and to anyone working on Thinkerwell’s behalf.
privacy.learnersBody: Use a nickname, avoid sharing sensitive personal information, and remember that others using your device may see your saved work. You can skip uncomfortable questions and ask a trusted adult for help.

s1.title: 1. Information and privacy
s1.p1: Learner profiles, preferences, progress and journal responses are saved in the browser on the device used. Shared-device profiles should not be treated as password-protected accounts. Avoid entering addresses, contact details, identity documents or sensitive family information into learning activities.
s1.p2: If you contact us, we receive the information you choose to provide, such as your email address and message. Website hosting and external services may also process technical information, including IP addresses and browser details. Thinkerwell uses information only for the purposes described in this policy.

s2.title: 2. How information is used
s2.p1: We limit personal information to what is necessary to provide learning, operate and secure Thinkerwell, respond to enquiries and address safety concerns. We do not sell learners’ personal information or distribute it for advertising or unrelated purposes. Limited sharing is restricted to the service, safeguarding and legal purposes described here. We do not use personal information for targeted advertising or identifiable learner work to train third-party, non-local AI models.
s2.stats: We will collect anonymised, aggregated numerical statistics about platform usage and engagement, such as total visits, lesson activity and feature usage. These statistics help us understand Thinkerwell’s reach and improve the learning experience. They will exclude names, contact details and journal content, and will not identify individual learners. We will not attempt to re-identify anyone from this information.
s2.statsNow: Thinkerwell does not collect these statistics yet. Nothing on the site counts visits, lessons or features today.
s2.coded: An optional feature for pilot partners could link usage data to learner codes. It is switched off for everyone, and nothing is collected through it. Coded data is not anonymous, so it is separate from the statistics above. Any pilot data collection is agreed with each organisation first, with the permissions it needs.
s2.p3: Where consent is required, we explain the purpose clearly and obtain appropriate consent, including from a parent or legal guardian for children under 13 and whenever otherwise required.

s3.title: 3. External services
s3.p1: Audio, embedded videos and external links may involve other providers, whose privacy practices also apply. We identify relevant providers, cookies or analytics and explain what information they receive. Providers handling information on our behalf must receive only what they need, with appropriate safeguards, including for overseas processing.
s3.whoIntro: These are the only services that receive information from using Thinkerwell. Thinkerwell does not set cookies, and has no ads or analytics from other companies.
s3.retention: Thinkerwell’s own server keeps nothing from the contact form. Copies held by the email services are kept only as long as needed to answer, then deleted. Hosting records are kept by the hosting provider as its policy describes.
s3.deviceTitle: Handled on the device, not sent to a service
s3.device1: Saved work. Profiles, preferences, progress, journal responses and the latest speaking recording stay in the browser’s storage on the device (IndexedDB, with a few small settings in local storage). Nothing is uploaded.
s3.device2: Listen. It reads lessons aloud with recordings delivered with the site, or with a voice already on the device. No lesson text or learner writing is sent to a voice service.
s3.device3: Record yourself. The microphone is used only when a learner taps Start. The clip stays on the device and is never uploaded.
s3.device4: Fonts, pictures and audio. They come from Thinkerwell’s own servers.
s3.device5: AI. No AI service receives learner information. The pretend tool in the Digital World course gives pre-written answers.

vercel.name: Vercel (website hosting)
vercel.purpose: Delivers the website and its files.
vercel.gets: Like any web server, it sees the IP address, browser and device details, and the pages requested.
vercel.where: Vercel runs servers in several countries, so this may be processed outside the country you are in.

resend.name: Resend (contact form delivery)
resend.purpose: Sends messages from the contact form to our team.
resend.gets: What you type in the form: the topic, your name, your email address or WhatsApp number, and your message.
resend.where: Resend may process it outside the country you are in.

google.name: Google (our email inbox)
google.purpose: Holds the team’s inbox, so we can read and answer you.
google.gets: Every email you send us, and the messages from the contact form.
google.where: Google processes information in many countries.

youtube.name: YouTube (optional videos)
youtube.purpose: Plays a lesson video, only after a learner taps play. Every video has a written version.
youtube.gets: The player comes from youtube-nocookie.com. Once a video plays, YouTube receives the IP address and browser details, and may use cookies or similar storage on the device.
youtube.where: Google processes information in many countries.

speech.name: Your browser’s speech service (only if turned on)
speech.purpose: Turns speech into text for the Say it button.
speech.gets: Off unless an educator turns on “Allow online speech-to-text” in Settings. When it is on, what a learner says is sent to the browser maker’s service.
speech.where: This depends on the browser. Read its maker’s privacy policy.

s4.title: 4. Security, retention and choices
s4.p1: We restrict access to information we hold and use reasonable security measures. We retain it only as long as needed for its stated purpose or legal obligations, then delete or anonymise it. If a data breach occurs, we assess it and notify affected people and authorities where required.
s4.p2: Contact us to request access, correction, deletion or withdrawal of consent. We will explain any applicable limits. Clearing Thinkerwell’s browser data can remove all locally saved profiles and work on that browser. We cannot remotely retrieve or erase information held only on your device. Others with access to that browser may still be able to see it.
s4.remove: On the “Who’s learning today?” screen, Remove deletes one learner’s lesson work, journal, section check scores and recordings from that device. It cannot be undone.

s5.title: 5. Keeping children safe
s5.p1: We prohibit abuse, exploitation, harassment, bullying and discrimination. Team members must follow safeguarding conduct rules and receive preparation and suitability checks appropriate to their roles. Direct learner sessions must have responsible adult supervision; secret contact and unsupervised private sessions are prohibited.
s5.p2: We review materials for age suitability. Learners and organisations may skip sensitive activities or use fictional examples without sharing personal experiences. Partners and Thinkerwell must agree on supervision, consent and local reporting arrangements before joint activities.

s6.title: 6. Images, recordings and stories
s6.p1: We do not routinely record learner sessions. Using identifiable images, recordings, quotations or work requires specific parent or guardian permission and the child’s agreement. Refusing does not affect learning access. Permission never justifies material that could put a child at risk.

s7.title: 7. Questions and concerns
s7.p1: Contact {email} for privacy requests, unsuitable content or safeguarding concerns. Share only necessary details. Reports will be taken seriously, handled without retaliation and shared only with people who need to respond. Absolute secrecy cannot be promised where protection or legal reporting requires disclosure. Concerns involving team members must receive independent handling.
s7.p2: Journals are not monitored for safety concerns, and our inbox is not an emergency service. For immediate danger, contact local emergency services or a safe, trusted adult.
s7.p3: We review this policy annually and after significant changes or incidents, and publish its latest revision date.
